aliases: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, Paris
tips.tip: Go right when you enter and ride the escalators up to the Impressionist galleries first — kids burn out fast if you start with the ground floor sculpture hall. The café behind the clock face is worth the detour for the view alone.
tips.author: Piotr

tips.tip: Wednesday evenings are quieter and often free for locals — check the AGO site before you go. Start in the contemporary wing upstairs; the Walker Court is a great reset spot between galleries.
tips.author: Piotr

tips.tip: Skip the classic counter line if you can — the cafe a block away takes walks-ins and has the same smoked fish, plus coffee. Order the super heebster and a chocolate egg cream; share plates so you can try more.
tips.author: Piotr

tips.tip: The iced coffee is especially amazing. They put a huge block of ice in it and it just hits the spot in the summertime. Grab a beverage for yourself and an ice pop or pastry for the kids and head over to one of the nearby parks on the lake to enjoy them.
tips.author: Piotr

tips.placeName: The Meadows at Lake Saint Louis
aliases: The Meadows at Lake Saint Louis
10 Meadow Cir Dr, Lake St Louis
tips.tip: There’s an amazing farmers market every Saturday between April 4 and October 31 from 8AM to noon. There’s vendors that sell produce, home made crafts, and food you can eat on the spot. There’s a playground too.
tips.author: Piotr

tips.tip:
The latest updates to the tower experience are great. Floor to ceiling windows, open air observation area, and the glass floor. There are two observation areas, the main one and the smaller observation deck above that. Dining at the 360 restaurant gives you access to the observation deck as well. The food isn’t bad but you might just consider getting a drink and enjoying the view.

When you’re in the area, walk over to Roundhouse Park to see historic trains and then have lunch at Steam Whistle Brewery.
tips.author: Piotr
